conventions.convention: Moment data have a<b, integer m≥1, r∈{2m−1,2m}, a finite positive measure on the relative Borel sigma-algebra of [a,b], positive total mass, and relative support containing at least m+1 distinct points.
The moment pairing is defined on coefficient vectors for degrees k≤m with 2k≤r. The exactness branch constructs p_m without assuming its squared norm; the remainder branch uses r=2m.
Orthogonal polynomials are monic, p_0=1, and p_j is orthogonal to every polynomial of degree less than j; the j=0 condition is vacuous.
Gaussian nodes are increasingly ordered interior roots; weights are integrals of cardinal polynomials, and the rule accepts any real-valued function defined at those nodes.
Tensor polynomials include their real coefficient families as formal data. Multi-indices are summed in increasing lexicographic order, and coordinate products use increasing coordinate order; d≥1.
The finite product measure is formed by binary products iterated from left to right on the relative Borel interval spaces; probability normalization is unnecessary.

Certified Golub–Welsch assumes truthful moment intervals. Its eigensolver supplies proposals only; failed checks return inconclusive. The m=1 branch requires no projected eigensolver, and successful enclosure is not promised for every requested tolerance.
The Gauss–Legendre example explicitly assumes Countable Choice for the library's Lebesgue-measure construction and Riemann–Lebesgue comparison.

load_bearing.statement: For a<b, m≥1 and r∈{2m−1,2m}, a Gaussian moment datum is a finite positive relative Borel measure of positive mass, with relative support containing at least m+1 points and finite absolute moments through r.
For moment data with r≥2m−1, each j=0,…,m has a unique monic real polynomial p_j of degree j orthogonal to every real polynomial of degree less than j. For j=0, p_0=1 and orthogonality is vacuous.
For moment data and 0≤k≤m with 2k≤r, the polynomial moment pairing is a well-defined real inner product on R^(k+1).
For moment data with r≥2m−1, p_m has exactly m distinct simple roots a<x_1<⋯<x_m<b, and p_m(X)=∏(X−x_i).
For order-(2m−1) moment data, the Gaussian rule equals the integral for every real polynomial of degree at most 2m−1; every weight is strictly positive and their sum is μ([a,b]).
For 0≤j<m, h_j=∫p_j²dμ>0 and α_j=∫xp_j²dμ/h_j are defined; β_j=h_j/h_(j−1)>0 for 1≤j<m. The recurrence is xp_0=p_1+α_0p_0 and xp_j=p_(j+1)+α_jp_j+β_jp_(j−1).
The real symmetric Jacobi matrix has precisely the Gaussian nodes as eigenvalues, all simple; evaluation vectors of the normalized polynomials are nonzero eigenvectors at those nodes.

For m distinct interior nodes and real f∈C^(2m)([a,b]), the displayed Hermite polynomial has degree at most 2m−1 and matches f and f′ at each node. At every non-node x∈[a,b], its error is f^(2m)(ξ_x)∏(x−x_i)²/(2m)! for some ξ_x∈(a,b).
For any unit Jacobi eigenvector v_i belonging to Gaussian node x_i, w_i=μ([a,b])|v_(i,1)|².

For Gaussian coordinate data, every real coordinatewise tensor polynomial is integrable under the finite product measure and its integral equals I_⊗(P); the conclusion also applies to probability marginals.

concerns.concern: F4 and Proof 1.1 write f=p_m s+t with “deg s<m”, allowing t=0 explicitly but omitting the analogous s=0 case. For example, f=1 gives s=0 for every m≥1, and def-real-polynomial-degree-leading-coefficient-and-monic explicitly gives the zero polynomial no degree. State “s=0 or deg s<m” and treat its orthogonality integral as zero. This is an immediate zero-case clarification; the exactness conclusion remains sound.

seams_checked.note: Cardinal values, degree bounds, interpolation uniqueness, linear-factor products and highest derivatives are used within their stated domains. The Hermite proof creates distinct zeros of g′ before applying the distinct-zero higher-order Rolle theorem.

Golub–Welsch supplies full interval families to the uniform linear certifier and a Hermitian family to the ordered eigenvalue certifier. Its soundness proof uses their conditional certified-output guarantees, including ordered eigenvalue containment, without asserting eventual certification.

The proposal call uses full dimension m, target count m−1, a finite-return projected eigensolver provider, a finite restart budget and an explicit thick-restart target rule. Unavailable, invalid and nonconverged outputs become inconclusive; exact Ritz data are independently checked before interval certification.

The unit-interval supplier establishes order-2M data under Countable Choice. The midpoint and weighted-defect consumers explicitly pass to the lower moment branch, identify the same polynomial by uniqueness, and identify Riemann tableau weights with Lebesgue Gaussian weights. The remainder is applied componentwise to C^(2M) scalar functions.
